question: A basin study compares dry weather flow with flow during storms. Which input most directly identifies the rainfall dependent share of inflow and infiltration?
correctAnswer: Rain gauge records matched against the flow meter hydrograph
explanation: Matching rainfall timing and depth to the flow response separates rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration from base sanitary flow and steady groundwater infiltration.
options: Pump run time totals collected at the nearest lift station over the same week
Rain gauge records matched against the flow meter hydrograph
CCTV defect counts taken from the oldest trunk sewer in the study basin
Customer billing totals for the basin during the same calendar month
optionA: Pump run time totals collected at the nearest lift station over the same week
optionB: Rain gauge records matched against the flow meter hydrograph
optionC: CCTV defect counts taken from the oldest trunk sewer in the study basin
optionD: Customer billing totals for the basin during the same calendar month
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: I&I Reduction Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: I&I Reduction Programs

question: A supervisor trends station performance month over month. Which record best shows whether a duty pump is gradually losing capacity?
correctAnswer: Drawdown test results trended against earlier tests at the same station
explanation: A drawdown test measures actual pumping rate under working conditions, so trending those results against earlier tests reveals capacity loss before it causes a failure.
options: Paint condition notes recorded during the annual station washdown visit
Fuel delivery receipts kept for the standby generator over the past winter
Drawdown test results trended against earlier tests at the same station
Visitor sign in sheets from contractor tours through the wet well area
optionA: Paint condition notes recorded during the annual station washdown visit
optionB: Fuel delivery receipts kept for the standby generator over the past winter
optionC: Drawdown test results trended against earlier tests at the same station
optionD: Visitor sign in sheets from contractor tours through the wet well area
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Lift Station Reliability Analysis.

question: A force main rises and falls along its route between the station and the discharge manhole. Where does air tend to collect while the main is pumping?
correctAnswer: At the high points along the force main profile
explanation: Air carried with the sewage rises and gathers at the high points of the profile, where it can restrict flow if it is not released.
options: At the high points along the force main profile
At the lowest point where the pipe passes under a creek crossing
Inside the wet well beside the pump discharge elbow connection
At the discharge manhole where the flow becomes gravity again
optionA: At the high points along the force main profile
optionB: At the lowest point where the pipe passes under a creek crossing
optionC: Inside the wet well beside the pump discharge elbow connection
optionD: At the discharge manhole where the flow becomes gravity again
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Force Main Management.
blueprintObjective: Lift Station Operation and Maintenance: Force Main Management

question: An air release valve sits at a force main high point. What does the valve release during normal pumping?
correctAnswer: Accumulated air that collects at the crown of the pipe
explanation: Air release valves vent air that gathers at the crown of the pipe at high points, keeping the full flow area available for sewage.
options: Treated effluent that bypasses the discharge manhole during peak flows
Hydrogen sulfide gas drawn from the gravity sewer downstream of the main
Grit and solids that settle out of the flow at the profile high point
Accumulated air that collects at the crown of the pipe
optionA: Treated effluent that bypasses the discharge manhole during peak flows
optionB: Hydrogen sulfide gas drawn from the gravity sewer downstream of the main
optionC: Grit and solids that settle out of the flow at the profile high point
optionD: Accumulated air that collects at the crown of the pipe
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Air Release Programs.
blueprintObjective: Equipment Operation & Maintenance: Air Release Programs

question: A long, flat gravity reach runs warm sewage at low velocity through summer. Which condition in that reach most promotes hydrogen sulfide generation?
correctAnswer: Long detention time with warm sewage and low dissolved oxygen
explanation: Sulfide generating bacteria thrive in the slime layer when sewage stays in the pipe a long time, is warm, and has little dissolved oxygen.
options: High velocity that keeps solids moving steadily through the reach
Cold sewage arriving from a short, steep upstream collector sewer
Long detention time with warm sewage and low dissolved oxygen
Frequent flushing that replaces the sewage in the reach every day
optionA: High velocity that keeps solids moving steadily through the reach
optionB: Cold sewage arriving from a short, steep upstream collector sewer
optionC: Long detention time with warm sewage and low dissolved oxygen
optionD: Frequent flushing that replaces the sewage in the reach every day
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Odour and Sulfide Corrosion Management.

question: A cafe kitchen wants to cut the fats, oils and grease reaching the sewer. Which practice most reduces that loading at the source?
correctAnswer: Scraping plates and trapping grease before wash water drains away
explanation: Source control works by keeping grease out of the drain in the first place, through scraping, dry cleanup and a properly used grease interceptor.
options: Running hotter water so grease stays liquid until it reaches the street main
Scraping plates and trapping grease before wash water drains away
Pouring used fryer oil into the floor drain at the end of each busy shift
Flushing the interceptor with detergent each night so grease moves downstream
optionA: Running hotter water so grease stays liquid until it reaches the street main
optionB: Scraping plates and trapping grease before wash water drains away
optionC: Pouring used fryer oil into the floor drain at the end of each busy shift
optionD: Flushing the interceptor with detergent each night so grease moves downstream
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: FOG Programs Depth.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: FOG Programs Depth

question: During a wet weather investigation, which private property connection acts as a direct inflow source when it rains?
correctAnswer: A foundation drain or downspout connected to the sanitary lateral
explanation: Roof leaders and foundation drains tied into the sanitary lateral deliver rain water straight into the collection system, adding inflow with every storm.
options: A weeping tile bed that discharges to a sump pit inside the basement
A garden hose bib on the side wall of the house facing the street
A water service line that runs beside the lateral in the same trench
A foundation drain or downspout connected to the sanitary lateral
optionA: A weeping tile bed that discharges to a sump pit inside the basement
optionB: A garden hose bib on the side wall of the house facing the street
optionC: A water service line that runs beside the lateral in the same trench
optionD: A foundation drain or downspout connected to the sanitary lateral
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: A resident phones in a sewage overflow at a manhole near a park. What must the response plan give the person who takes that first call?
correctAnswer: The notification sequence, starting with the supervisor and the spill reporting contact
explanation: A written notification sequence makes sure supervisors and the provincial spill reporting contact are reached quickly and in the right order, every time.
options: The notification sequence, starting with the supervisor and the spill reporting contact
The home phone numbers of every crew member who lives near the park entrance
A script for telling the caller the overflow will be cleaned within the hour
Directions to the nearest rental yard for extra bypass pumps and hose reels
optionA: The notification sequence, starting with the supervisor and the spill reporting contact
optionB: The home phone numbers of every crew member who lives near the park entrance
optionC: A script for telling the caller the overflow will be cleaned within the hour

question: A crew smoke tests a block before a lining project. Smoke pours from a roof vent stack and a downspout on one house. What does that finding tell the crew?
correctAnswer: A roof drain or downspout on that property is connected to the sanitary sewer
explanation: Smoke follows the path of connected piping, so smoke at roof drainage points shows those fixtures drain to the sanitary system and add inflow when it rains.
options: A roof drain or downspout on that property is connected to the sanitary sewer
The house lateral is blocked somewhere below the foundation wall of the home
Groundwater is entering the street main through a cracked joint near the house
The street main needs jet cleaning before any lining work can proceed there
optionA: A roof drain or downspout on that property is connected to the sanitary sewer
optionB: The house lateral is blocked somewhere below the foundation wall of the home
optionC: Groundwater is entering the street main through a cracked joint near the house

question: A station alternates its two pumps between duty and standby on a set schedule. What does that alternation accomplish?
correctAnswer: It equalizes wear and confirms both pumps stay ready to run
explanation: Alternating duty spreads run hours evenly and proves regularly that the standby pump starts and pumps when called on.
options: It keeps the wet well completely empty for longer stretches each shift
It reduces the number of level floats the station needs to carry
It lets one pump sit idle for a full week between operating runs
It equalizes wear and confirms both pumps stay ready to run
optionA: It keeps the wet well completely empty for longer stretches each shift
optionB: It reduces the number of level floats the station needs to carry
optionC: It lets one pump sit idle for a full week between operating runs
optionD: It equalizes wear and confirms both pumps stay ready to run

question: Discharge pressure at a station has crept upward over several months while the pump rate stays about the same. What does that trend most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: A partial restriction or trapped air is developing inside the force main
explanation: Rising pressure at a steady flow means the main is offering more resistance, which points to a growing restriction or air binding at a high point.
options: The wet well has become larger than the original design drawings indicate
A partial restriction or trapped air is developing inside the force main
The discharge manhole has been raised by a recent road resurfacing project
The check valves have started opening wider than they did when installed
optionA: The wet well has become larger than the original design drawings indicate
optionB: A partial restriction or trapped air is developing inside the force main
optionC: The discharge manhole has been raised by a recent road resurfacing project
optionD: The check valves have started opening wider than they did when installed
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: An air release valve that has not been serviced in years is found stuck closed. Which operating problem develops first at that high point?
correctAnswer: Air accumulates at the high point and shrinks the effective flow area
explanation: With the valve stuck shut, air keeps collecting at the crown, narrowing the passage and raising the head the pumps must work against.
options: Sewage backs up into the wet well and floods the station dry pit floor
The pump motors begin drawing less current and run cooler than normal
Air accumulates at the high point and shrinks the effective flow area
The discharge manhole surcharges because the gravity sewer is oversized
optionA: Sewage backs up into the wet well and floods the station dry pit floor
optionB: The pump motors begin drawing less current and run cooler than normal
optionC: Air accumulates at the high point and shrinks the effective flow area
optionD: The discharge manhole surcharges because the gravity sewer is oversized
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Air Release Programs.
blueprintObjective: Equipment Operation & Maintenance: Air Release Programs

question: In a corroded manhole, the concrete loss is worst on the wall just above the flow line rather than below it. Why does the damage concentrate there?
correctAnswer: Sulfide gas released from the flow is converted to acid on the moist wall above the waterline
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide leaves the sewage, and bacteria on the damp wall above the flow convert it to sulfuric acid, which eats into the concrete at that band.
options: Chloride rich groundwater seeps through the benching and attacks the concrete from behind the wall
Grit carried in the flow scours the wall surface each time the sewer surcharges during a storm
Freeze and thaw cycles split the wall surface where condensation forms during the winter months
Sulfide gas released from the flow is converted to acid on the moist wall above the waterline
optionA: Chloride rich groundwater seeps through the benching and attacks the concrete from behind the wall
optionB: Grit carried in the flow scours the wall surface each time the sewer surcharges during a storm
optionC: Freeze and thaw cycles split the wall surface where condensation forms during the winter months
optionD: Sulfide gas released from the flow is converted to acid on the moist wall above the waterline
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Odour and Sulfide Corrosion Management.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Odour and Sulfide Corrosion Management

question: A restaurant interceptor passes its inspection, yet the main downstream still builds up grease between cleanings. What should the program check next?
correctAnswer: Whether the interceptor is pumped out before accumulated grease fills its working capacity
explanation: An interceptor only works while it has room to separate and hold grease; once accumulated grease and solids fill its working capacity, grease passes straight through.
options: Whether the interceptor is pumped out before accumulated grease fills its working capacity
Whether the restaurant washes its floors more often than the program schedule assumes
Whether the street main was jetted with enough pressure during the last cleaning visit
Whether the menu at the restaurant has added fried items since the last inspection
optionA: Whether the interceptor is pumped out before accumulated grease fills its working capacity
optionB: Whether the restaurant washes its floors more often than the program schedule assumes
optionC: Whether the street main was jetted with enough pressure during the last cleaning visit
optionD: Whether the menu at the restaurant has added fried items since the last inspection
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: FOG Programs Depth.

question: A homeowner refuses access for a lateral inspection the program needs. What is the usual next step for the crew?
correctAnswer: Document the refusal and assess the lateral from public access using mainline CCTV and dye testing
explanation: Programs respect property access, record the refusal, and use tools that work from the public side, such as mainline cameras and dye introduced at public fixtures.
options: Enter the property anyway, since the lateral connects to a public sewer main in the street
Remove the property from the basin study and report its flows as if they were zero
Document the refusal and assess the lateral from public access using mainline CCTV and dye testing
Fine the homeowner on the spot and schedule the inspection for the following week
optionA: Enter the property anyway, since the lateral connects to a public sewer main in the street
optionB: Remove the property from the basin study and report its flows as if they were zero
optionC: Document the refusal and assess the lateral from public access using mainline CCTV and dye testing
optionD: Fine the homeowner on the spot and schedule the inspection for the following week

question: Sewage is surfacing from a manhole and flowing toward a creek during a storm. What is the first field action for the responding crew?
correctAnswer: Contain the spill and protect the watercourse while notifications are made
explanation: Stopping sewage from reaching the watercourse limits environmental damage, and containment goes in while the notification sequence runs at the same time.
options: Begin excavating to find the break before setting out any containment gear
Contain the spill and protect the watercourse while notifications are made
Photograph the scene for the report and leave the flow until the storm passes
Open the downstream manholes so the surfacing sewage drains back into the sewer
optionA: Begin excavating to find the break before setting out any containment gear
optionB: Contain the spill and protect the watercourse while notifications are made
optionC: Photograph the scene for the report and leave the flow until the storm passes

question: A night flow study in a residential basin shows the minimum flow between 2 and 4 in the morning stays high even after a week without rain. What does that pattern point to?
correctAnswer: Groundwater infiltration entering through defects below the water table
explanation: With residents asleep and no rain, sanitary flow should fall to a low base; a stubbornly high dry weather night flow is the classic signature of groundwater infiltration.
options: Direct storm connections that respond only while rain is actually falling
Groundwater infiltration entering through defects below the water table
Industrial discharges that peak during weekday production hours at the plant
Lift station cycling that lifts flows in short, regular bursts all night
optionA: Direct storm connections that respond only while rain is actually falling
optionB: Groundwater infiltration entering through defects below the water table
optionC: Industrial discharges that peak during weekday production hours at the plant
optionD: Lift station cycling that lifts flows in short, regular bursts all night
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: A pump trips on high motor temperature twice in one week, and its check valve has started to slam. What should the operator do first?
correctAnswer: Log both events and inspect the pump and check valve before returning the station to normal rotation
explanation: Repeated trips and a slamming valve are early failure warnings; recording them and inspecting the equipment protects the station from an unplanned outage.
options: Reset the trip both times and wait to see whether a third trip happens before reporting anything
Swap the pump to standby permanently and leave the faulty unit in place until the annual overhaul
Log both events and inspect the pump and check valve before returning the station to normal rotation
Raise the high level alarm setpoint so the pump runs less often and stays cooler between cycles
optionA: Reset the trip both times and wait to see whether a third trip happens before reporting anything
optionB: Swap the pump to standby permanently and leave the faulty unit in place until the annual overhaul
optionC: Log both events and inspect the pump and check valve before returning the station to normal rotation
optionD: Raise the high level alarm setpoint so the pump runs less often and stays cooler between cycles

question: A crew plans to swab a force main to restore its capacity. Which step must be settled before the swab is launched?
correctAnswer: Isolation points and a receiving plan for the surge and material at the discharge end
explanation: A swab arrives with a surge of flow and dislodged material, so isolation, receiving capacity and disposal must be arranged before it is sent.
options: The paint colour for the valve chamber covers once the swabbing work is finished
A new duty roster for the station so both pumps can rest during the swab run
The order in which the gravity sewers downstream will be televised next season
Isolation points and a receiving plan for the surge and material at the discharge end

question: A force main is drained down for a repair. Which valve function protects the pipe from damage caused by negative pressure during that draining?
correctAnswer: The vacuum relief function, which admits air as internal pressure drops
explanation: Combination air valves admit air when pressure inside the main falls, preventing vacuum conditions that can damage or collapse the pipe.
options: The vacuum relief function, which admits air as internal pressure drops
The pressure sustaining function, which holds back flow until a setpoint is reached
The surge anticipator function, which opens the pump discharge before start up
The float drain function, which empties the valve body between service visits
optionA: The vacuum relief function, which admits air as internal pressure drops
optionB: The pressure sustaining function, which holds back flow until a setpoint is reached
optionC: The surge anticipator function, which opens the pump discharge before start up
optionD: The float drain function, which empties the valve body between service visits

question: Residents report rotten egg odours near a discharge manhole on warm evenings. Which check should the operator make first?
correctAnswer: Measure hydrogen sulfide at the manhole and review detention time in the force main feeding it
explanation: Odour at a force main discharge usually means sulfide built up during long detention in the main, so gas readings and detention review confirm the cause before money is spent.
options: Replace the manhole cover with a sealed unit and close the file until complaints come in again
Flush the gravity sewer downstream with hydrant water every evening for the rest of the summer
Measure hydrogen sulfide at the manhole and review detention time in the force main feeding it
Ask residents to keep windows closed and log the complaint as a seasonal nuisance condition
optionA: Replace the manhole cover with a sealed unit and close the file until complaints come in again
optionB: Flush the gravity sewer downstream with hydrant water every evening for the rest of the summer
optionC: Measure hydrogen sulfide at the manhole and review detention time in the force main feeding it
optionD: Ask residents to keep windows closed and log the complaint as a seasonal nuisance condition

question: A new restaurant opens in a plaza but never appears in the FOG program records, and grease problems start downstream. Which program step failed?
correctAnswer: The source inventory step that identifies and registers food service establishments
explanation: A FOG program can only inspect and track establishments it knows about, so a missed registration is a failure of the source inventory, not of field cleaning.
options: The jetting schedule step that sets cleaning frequency for the plaza sewer lateral
The sampling step that measures effluent quality at the treatment plant headworks
The billing step that adds the new tenant to the water utility customer accounts
The source inventory step that identifies and registers food service establishments
optionA: The jetting schedule step that sets cleaning frequency for the plaza sewer lateral
optionB: The sampling step that measures effluent quality at the treatment plant headworks
optionC: The billing step that adds the new tenant to the water utility customer accounts

question: During smoke testing, smoke rises from a yard cleanout and also from a driveway catch basin on the same property. What does that combination suggest?
correctAnswer: The property has a cross connection that lets storm water reach the sanitary lateral
explanation: Smoke should never appear at a storm drainage structure; when it does, the storm and sanitary sides are connected somewhere on the property.
options: The property has a cross connection that lets storm water reach the sanitary lateral
The lateral has a sag that holds water and blocks smoke from travelling any farther
The street main is surcharged, pushing smoke back up through every opening on the lot
The catch basin is connected to the water service trench that runs beside the lateral
optionA: The property has a cross connection that lets storm water reach the sanitary lateral
optionB: The lateral has a sag that holds water and blocks smoke from travelling any farther
optionC: The street main is surcharged, pushing smoke back up through every opening on the lot
optionD: The catch basin is connected to the water service trench that runs beside the lateral

question: A trunk sewer breaks and a bypass pumping setup is being sized. Which factor sets how much bypass capacity is needed?
correctAnswer: The peak flow the bypass must carry until the repair is complete
explanation: The bypass has to pass the sewer flow, including its peak, for the whole repair period, so peak flow is the sizing basis.
options: The number of traffic cones available for closing the street at the site
The peak flow the bypass must carry until the repair is complete
The distance from the depot to the break, measured along the haul route
The age of the trunk sewer, taken from the oldest record in the asset file
optionA: The number of traffic cones available for closing the street at the site

question: Basin A has the highest infiltration rate per hectare but a small area, while Basin B has a moderate rate over a large area and its trunk surcharges in storms. Which basin should the rehabilitation program take first?
correctAnswer: Basin B, because its excess flow is the one driving surcharge and overflow risk
explanation: Programs rank work by consequence as well as rate; the basin whose extra flow surcharges the trunk and threatens overflows delivers the most risk reduction per dollar.
options: Basin B, because its excess flow is the one driving surcharge and overflow risk
Basin A, because the highest rate per hectare is always the first priority in any program
Neither basin, until every basin in the system has been flow monitored for a full year
Both basins at once, splitting the lining contract evenly regardless of the flow results
optionA: Basin B, because its excess flow is the one driving surcharge and overflow risk
optionB: Basin A, because the highest rate per hectare is always the first priority in any program
optionC: Neither basin, until every basin in the system has been flow monitored for a full year
optionD: Both basins at once, splitting the lining contract evenly regardless of the flow results
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: During a power outage the generator runs, but it can carry only one pump and the wet well level keeps rising. Which design shortcoming does that expose?
correctAnswer: The standby power supply was not sized to carry the full duty pumping load
explanation: Reliability means the station keeps pumping through an outage; a generator that cannot run the duty load lets the well fill no matter how well it starts.
options: The wet well was built with more storage volume than the design drawings required
The standby power supply was not sized to carry the full duty pumping load
The level floats were set too far apart when the station was first commissioned
The discharge check valves were installed facing the wrong direction on the header
optionA: The wet well was built with more storage volume than the design drawings required
optionB: The standby power supply was not sized to carry the full duty pumping load
optionC: The level floats were set too far apart when the station was first commissioned
optionD: The discharge check valves were installed facing the wrong direction on the header
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Lift Station Reliability Analysis.

question: A pump shuts down suddenly at a station with a long force main. What protects the main from the pressure surge that follows the sudden stop?
correctAnswer: A surge relief device or air chamber that absorbs the pressure wave
explanation: When flow stops abruptly, the moving column rebounds as a pressure wave; surge relief devices and air chambers absorb that energy before it can split the pipe.
options: A second check valve installed in series right at the pump discharge elbow
A taller vent stack mounted on the first manhole past the discharge point
A thicker layer of bedding sand placed under the main during construction
A surge relief device or air chamber that absorbs the pressure wave
optionA: A second check valve installed in series right at the pump discharge elbow
optionB: A taller vent stack mounted on the first manhole past the discharge point
optionC: A thicker layer of bedding sand placed under the main during construction
optionD: A surge relief device or air chamber that absorbs the pressure wave
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: After a force main repair, the crew refills the main slowly rather than at full pump rate. Why does the slow refill matter?
correctAnswer: Slow filling lets air escape through the air valves instead of being trapped and compressed
explanation: Refilling too fast traps pockets of air that compress and surge; a controlled fill vents air through the valves as the water front advances.
options: Slow filling gives the pipe bedding time to dry out before the main returns to full service
Slow filling keeps the wet well level high enough for the pumps to prime on the next cycle
Slow filling lets air escape through the air valves instead of being trapped and compressed
Slow filling prevents the new gaskets from seating, so leaks show up during the pressure test
optionA: Slow filling gives the pipe bedding time to dry out before the main returns to full service
optionB: Slow filling keeps the wet well level high enough for the pumps to prime on the next cycle
optionC: Slow filling lets air escape through the air valves instead of being trapped and compressed
optionD: Slow filling prevents the new gaskets from seating, so leaks show up during the pressure test
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: Nitrate is dosed into a force main to control sulfide. How does the nitrate accomplish that control?
correctAnswer: It gives bacteria an alternate oxygen source, so they produce far less sulfide
explanation: Bacteria use nitrate in preference to sulfate when it is available, which cuts the amount of hydrogen sulfide they generate in the main.
options: It coats the pipe wall with a film that sulfide gas cannot pass through at all
It raises the sewage temperature so sulfide forming bacteria cannot survive
It neutralizes acid in the gravity sewer by raising the pH of the flow there
It gives bacteria an alternate oxygen source, so they produce far less sulfide
optionA: It coats the pipe wall with a film that sulfide gas cannot pass through at all
optionB: It raises the sewage temperature so sulfide forming bacteria cannot survive
optionC: It neutralizes acid in the gravity sewer by raising the pH of the flow there
optionD: It gives bacteria an alternate oxygen source, so they produce far less sulfide
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Cleaning records show the same two reaches below a food court are jetted every six weeks, year after year. Which decision best addresses the pattern?
correctAnswer: Target inspection and enforcement at the food service sources upstream of those reaches
explanation: Repeat cleaning at the same spots is a symptom; a FOG program reduces the work by fixing the source loading coming from the establishments upstream.
options: Keep jetting on the same six week cycle, since the reaches have not blocked completely yet
Upsize both reaches to the next pipe diameter so the grease has more room to accumulate
Target inspection and enforcement at the food service sources upstream of those reaches
Move the jetting to a different pair of reaches so the work is spread across the system

optionB: Upsize both reaches to the next pipe diameter so the grease has more room to accumulate

question: A municipality offers cost sharing for private lateral repairs. Which eligibility rule best targets the public benefit of the program?
correctAnswer: Fund repairs where the lateral defect contributes measured inflow or infiltration to the public system
explanation: Public money follows public benefit; tying eligibility to a measured contribution to system flows spends it where the collection system actually gains.

Fund only laterals on streets where a lining contract is already scheduled for the same season
Fund repairs in the order applications arrive, without checking what the defect contributes

question: After lining and lateral sealing in a basin, the wet weather peak flow drops sharply, but the dry weather night flow barely changes. How should the operator interpret that result?
correctAnswer: Rainfall dependent inflow sources were reduced, but groundwater infiltration is still entering
explanation: Peak flow responds to direct inflow sources, while steady night flow reflects groundwater entering through remaining defects, so the two results describe two different sources.
options: The lining made the infiltration worse, and the night flow proves the project failed overall
Rainfall dependent inflow sources were reduced, but groundwater infiltration is still entering
The flow meter drifted during the project, so neither result can be trusted for the report
Groundwater infiltration was eliminated, and the remaining night flow is all sanitary base flow

optionB: Rainfall dependent inflow sources were reduced, but groundwater infiltration is still entering

question: Run hour meters show one pump has taken about 80 percent of the starts over the last quarter, though the station is set to alternate. What does that imbalance most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: The alternation control or lead pump selection is failing to switch duty between the pumps
explanation: Alternation is a control function; when one pump consistently takes most starts, the switching control, a relay or a float input is not doing its job.
options: The alternation control or lead pump selection is failing to switch duty between the pumps
The wet well has grown larger over the quarter, so one pump can now handle most of the flow
The discharge header has partially plugged, forcing the stronger pump to take the extra starts
The run hour meter on the second pump is wired to the wrong motor and under counts its hours

question: Two parallel force mains serve a station, and one is taken out of service for a repair. What happens inside the main that stays in service?
correctAnswer: Velocity and friction loss rise in the operating main, raising discharge pressure at the station
explanation: The full station flow now passes through one pipe instead of two, so velocity climbs and friction loss climbs with it, which the pumps feel as higher discharge pressure.
options: Velocity falls in the operating main because the pumps slow down to match the single pipe
Air pockets disappear from the operating main because all the flow now takes the shorter path
Velocity and friction loss rise in the operating main, raising discharge pressure at the station
The operating main begins to run by gravity because its twin is no longer pressurized
optionA: Velocity falls in the operating main because the pumps slow down to match the single pipe
optionB: Air pockets disappear from the operating main because all the flow now takes the shorter path
optionC: Velocity and friction loss rise in the operating main, raising discharge pressure at the station
optionD: The operating main begins to run by gravity because its twin is no longer pressurized

question: The first two manholes below a force main discharge are corroding rapidly. Which change attacks the cause rather than the symptom?

explanation: Corrosion at the discharge starts with sulfide formed during detention in the main; cutting detention or dosing at the station reduces the sulfide itself, not just its effects.

Sealing the manhole covers tightly so the sulfide gas stays inside the sewer for a longer period of time

Scheduling odour complaint visits for cooler morning hours when the smell bothers residents the least

topic: Wet Well and Pump Capacity Analysis
question: A rectangular wet well is 3.0 m long and 2.5 m wide, with an operating band of 1.2 m between the pump off and pump on levels. Sewage enters at 40 L/s while the duty pump discharges 65 L/s. How long does the pump run to draw the band down? Round to 1 decimal place.
correctAnswer: 6.0 min
explanation: t = (L x W x band x 1000) / (Qpump - Qinflow) / 60. Substitute the stated values: (3.0 x 2.5 x 1.2 x 1000) / (65 - 40) / 60 = 9000 / 25 / 60 = 6.0 min. The band holds 9000 L and the pump gains on the inflow by 25 L/s. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.
formula: t = (L x W x band x 1000) / (Qpump - Qinflow) / 60
options: 2.3 min
5.0 min
6.0 min
7.5 min
optionA: 2.3 min
optionB: 5.0 min
optionC: 6.0 min
optionD: 7.5 min

question: A sewer runs 240 m between two manholes and the invert drops 1.2 m over that length. Flow through the reach is 84 L/s and the flow area is 0.07 m2. Using V = Q / A, with Q converted to m3/s, what is the velocity in the reach? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: V = (Q / 1000) / A. Substitute the stated values: (84 / 1000) / 0.07 = 0.084 / 0.07 = 1.2 m/s. The invert drop describes the slope of the reach and is not part of the continuity calculation. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

topic: Wet Well and Pump Capacity Analysis
question: A wet well is 4.0 m long and 3.0 m wide with a 0.8 m operating band. Inflow is 40 L/s and the pump discharges 120 L/s. The pump cycle is the fill time with the pump off plus the run time with the pump on. How many complete cycles run in one hour at this steady inflow? Round to 1 decimal place.
correctAnswer: 10.0 cycles/hour
explanation: Band volume = 4.0 x 3.0 x 0.8 x 1000 = 9600 L. Fill time = 9600 / 40 / 60 = 4.0 min and run time = 9600 / (120 - 40) / 60 = 2.0 min, so one cycle takes 6.0 min and 60 / 6.0 = 10.0 cycles/hour. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.
formula: Cycles per hour = 60 / (fill minutes + run minutes); fill = V / Qinflow; run = V / (Qpump - Qinflow)

10.0 cycles/hour

question: Peak inflow to a station reaches 90 L/s. The usable wet well volume between the pump off and pump on levels is 13.5 m3, and the pump must draw that band down in no more than 3 minutes while the peak inflow continues. What minimum pump rate is required? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: Qpump = (V x 1000 / t) + Qinflow. Substitute the stated values: (13.5 x 1000 / 180) + 90 = 75 + 90 = 165.0 L/s. The pump must remove the band volume in 180 seconds and also keep up with the 90 L/s still arriving. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.
